primarySourceContext.title: Microsoft Direct3D9 rasterization rules
primarySourceContext.support: D3D9 uses integer pixel centers and top-left coverage. The documentation allows small hardware variations; it does not prescribe the exact arithmetic of this captured driver.

primarySourceContext.title: Microsoft Direct3D9 viewports and clipping
primarySourceContext.support: The documented viewport map includes width/height scaling, top-left Y reversal and homogeneous coordinates before conversion. This establishes the real-number map, not a specific float evaluation order.

primarySourceContext.title: Microsoft D3D11.3 Functional Specification
primarySourceContext.support: On the ANGLE D3D11 side, XY positions are snapped to eight fractional bits before interpolator setup. Nearest-even conversion has a permitted 0.6 fixed-point ULP tolerance. Thus a one-grid-step vertex difference can change UV while preserving all integer sample coverage; this is an explanatory constraint, not proof of a D3D9 rounding implementation.

primarySourceContext.title: Khronos OpenGL ES3.0.6 specification
primarySourceContext.support: The specified conceptual path divides by clip W then maps NDC through viewport scale/center. Four reported subpixel bits are the ES minimum; they do not establish that this D3D11-backed capture rasterized at only four bits.

primarySourceContext.title: ANGLE DynamicHLSL.cpp reference revision chromium7479
primarySourceContext.support: The reference backend passes clip XY/W to D3D11, handles clip-control Y and Z, and has a separate lower-feature-level viewport-adjust path. This revision was read as primary source context; no installed browser version or executed branch was identified from this file.

conclusion: All three residual Native/portable differences are consistent with one isolated strip vertex crossing an eight-fractional-bit screen-coordinate boundary. Identical color/UV row-dot controls rule out a benefit from that syntax change on this captured driver. No tested offline viewport expression uniformly predicts every retained indirect Native corner estimate; further shader algebra trials need an actual backend arithmetic measurement rather than fitted corrections.
